result.title: When Local Semantics Disagree: Learning to Detect Fake News through Weakly Supervised Cross-Modal Reasoning
result.summary: The rapid proliferation of multimodal social media content has made fake news detection a pressing challenge for the vision-language community. Most existing approaches rely on coarse global similarity between text and images, which overlooks subtle, uneven cross-modal inconsistencies -- such as sentiment-scene mismatches, object-level manipulations, or semantic dissonance between visual and textual cues. Moreover, these models treat all inconsistencies as equally informative, ignoring domain-specific variation in how such conflicts manifest, which limits both generalization and interpretability. To address these challenges, we propose DMIL, a dual-branch multiple instance learning framework that formulates multimodal fake news detection as a weakly supervised learning problem. Each news article is treated as a bag of visual and textual instances processed through two complementary branches: an embedding-space branch that aggregates global semantics via expert-guided modality fusion, and an instance-space branch that models cross-modal inconsistencies across local-to-global granularities. A retrieval-augmented, domain-adaptive router further contextualizes inconsistencies using retrieved domain exemplars and dynamically fuses multi-level cues. Extensive experiments on public misinformation benchmarks demonstrate that DMIL achieves competitive state-of-the-art performance and demonstrates strong discriminative capability against fake news across different domains.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 DMIL 双分支多示例学习框架，把每条多模态新闻视为图文示例包，通过全局嵌入融合与局部到全局的跨模态不一致建模，并用检索增强的域自适应路由器融合多级线索，实现弱监督假新闻检测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其多示例式的局部证据聚合与路由器动态加权机制，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选和 latent 假设取舍提供线索，但该工作面向分类判别而非推理状态生成，需核查其不一致性分数能否用于停止或证据选择决策。
